subject: opencode wake re-injection (self-driving heartbeat via in-plugin SDK client)
description: Make the orchestrator heartbeat self-driving under opencode. Today schedule_wakeup arms a detached sleeper that writes ORCH_SCHEDULED_TASK to <data>/wake/<session>.fire, but nothing reads it back into the opencode session — so the loop ticks once then stalls. FIX: in-plugin reinjection. packages/opencode-plugin/zonoid.ts already receives `client: OpencodeClient` (from @opencode-ai/sdk) in its factory input; the SDK exposes client.session.promptAsync({path:{id:sessionId}, body:{parts:[{type:'text',text:prompt}]}}) -> POST /session/:id/prompt_async (204, no-wait). Add a per-session .fire watcher (fs.watch or polling; one per session, cancel-then-arm like the timer) that, on an ORCH_SCHEDULED_TASK line, parses the JSON payload and calls client.session.promptAsync with the prompt. Arm the watcher from the schedule_wakeup tool execute (it already has ctx.sessionID). Mirror lib/codex-wakeup-delivery.js + adapters/codex/wakeup-monitor.js as the structural reference, but do it IN-PLUGIN (no port discovery, no external process). Update docs/schedule-wakeup.md "OpenCode" row to note delivery is now in-plugin via the SDK client. Add a focused test for the fire-line parsing + a mocked client asserting promptAsync is called once with the parsed prompt. Verify by running test/cli-init.test.js + any opencode plugin tests.

summary:
OpenCode plugin now self-drives the heartbeat: schedule_wakeup arms both the substrate timer AND an in-plugin watcher that re-injects the fired prompt via the SDK client.

Changes:
- packages/opencode-plugin/zonoid.ts: factory now destructures `client` from PluginInput (was {directory,worktree} only); constructs `createWakeDelivery({ client })` once; after a successful armWakeup, calls `wakeDelivery.arm(session)` and adds `delivery:{supported, via:'sdk-promptAsync'}` to the tool return.
- packages/opencode-plugin/lib/wake-delivery.js (new): `createWakeDelivery({client, intervalMs=1000})` → `{arm, cancel}`. Reuses lib/schedule-wakeup.js fire-path helpers (fireFile/sessionSlug) — no hardcoded paths. One polling watcher per session (setInterval reader, byte-offset tracked, partial trailing line held back until newline). On each new `ORCH_SCHEDULED_TASK <json>` line: JSON.parse, extract `.prompt`, call `client.session.promptAsync({path:{id:session}, body:{parts:[{type:'text', text:prompt}]}})`. Best-effort: malformed JSON and delivery errors are swallowed, promise rejections drained. Dedup: a per-session processed-offset Map persists across cancel/arm, so a re-arm never re-fires an already-delivered line, while a first arm processes a pre-existing fire-line once. cancel-then-arm semantics; timer.unref()'d.
- docs/schedule-wakeup.md: "OpenCode plugin" row now notes in-plugin delivery via wake-delivery.js → SDK session.promptAsync (self-driving), not just arming.
- test/opencode-wake-delivery.test.js (new, 6 tests): pre-existing line fires exactly once with correct promptAsync shape; re-arm yields no duplicate; appended-after-arm line delivered; malformed JSON line skipped (no throw, only well-formed line delivered); arm without client returns ok:false (no throw); cancel-without-arm is a no-op.

SDK signature confirmed from ~/.config/opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/gen/types.gen.d.ts:
  client.session.promptAsync({ path:{id}, body:{ parts: Array<TextPartInput|
